info.bio:
Daryl Hall fundo el dúo musical más exitoso de la historia. Daryl Hall y John Oates, Hall y Oates, se anotaron un éxito tras otro durante los 70 y 80 con esas pegajosas baladas pop con aires soul. Fueron, por mucho, los reyes de un soul blanco bastante meloso. La base de su estilo era la combinación del falsete de Hall y barítono de Oates. 

Daryl Franklin Hohl nació el 11 de octubre de 1946 en Pottstown, Pensylvania y John Oates el 7 de abril de 1948 en Nueva York.

scenes.name: Techno-rock y pop de estudio
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El «sonido» por encima de la melodía, el ritmo y la armonía: Electric Light Orchestra inventa el «high-tech pop»; Supertramp, Alan Parsons Project, Kansas, Styx y Split Enz. El valor de la producción define a Steely Dan (el pop-jazz pulido de los yuppies), Hall & Oates, los Fleetwood Mac de Rumours y Tusk, Toto, el «muro de sonido» titánico de Jim Steinman (Bat Out Of Hell) y la Penguin Cafe Orchestra. A finales de los setenta, el art-rock culmina en los supergrupos: 10cc, Godley & Creme, Foreigner, UK, Asia, Sky.

podcast.title: Early Songwriting in Schubert Building
podcast.body: Daryl Hall and John Oates worked as songwriters in Philadelphia's Schubert building concurrently with Kenny Gamble and Leon Huff, indicating a shared early professional environment for these influential musicians. "Daryl Hall and John Oates were also working as songwriters in the Schubert building at the same time that Gamble and Huff were."

podcast.title: Influence of Kenny Gamble
podcast.body: Daryl Hall's musical sensibilities were shaped by the same types of music that influenced Kenny Gamble, pointing to a common foundation in soul and R&B traditions. "Daryl Hall, he was influenced by the same music as Kenny Gamble."

podcast.title: Philadelphia Native
podcast.body: Daryl Hall is a native of Philadelphia, and his musical background and influences are deeply rooted in the regional sounds that were foundational to Philly Soul. "Philly Native Daryl Hall"

podcast.title: Rejected PIR Contract
podcast.body: Hall and Oates were offered a recording contract by Gamble and Huff with Philadelphia International Records but chose to decline it, opting instead to relocate to New York to pursue a unique and independent musical direction. "Gamble and Huff did offer them a contract with PIR, but they wanted to do something a little different and went to New York to forge a different path."
